title: A Letter from the Ducal Chancery
sceneText:
The letter comes first thing. Not a courier — the duchy’s postman, who covers this part of the valley once a week, on Wednesdays.

The seal on the envelope is the chancery’s, not the Duke’s own.

variants.good:
To the Steward of Maplegate Estate.

Pursuant to this season’s summary of declared progress from the estates of the northern district, the autumn harvest and the preparation of dues at your estate are entered as ordinary. Dues payable this season will be assessed against the final harvest on the thirtieth of October.
variants.fair:
To the Steward of Maplegate Estate.

Pursuant to this season’s summary of declared progress from the estates of the northern district, the autumn harvest at your estate stands below the average for the district. Attention is directed to the provision of winter rations and of dues.
variants.poor:
To the Steward of Maplegate Estate.

Pursuant to this season’s summary of declared progress from the estates of the northern district, the autumn harvest at your estate is markedly in arrears. This office has forwarded a copy of the same to the lord of the estate.
variants.renewal:
Appended: the temporary residence and labour guarantee presently in force at your estate (no. VS-18-0947) expires on the thirtieth of October of this year. Should renewal be required, a document freshly signed by the guarantor must be submitted not later than seven days before expiry. Where no submission is made within that time, the holder is required under Chapter Fourteen of the Basic Law to depart the territory within seven days of expiry.

Chancery of the Duchy of Valewisp

The twenty-second of October
variants.after:
You read the letter twice.

The second part has nothing to do with the first. It is another matter altogether, written on the same sheet only because the same office sent it.

The thirtieth of October.

Until now you have been treating that number as a deadline for work. The harvest to be handed over, the books to balance, the estate to be got through the winter.

It is the deadline for something else at the same time.

You sit in the office a while. Out of the window Gregor is leading two horses out, and in the fields you can see the dark patches the frost leaves behind when it melts.

Eight days.
variants.broker:
That afternoon a man up from Valehold sends a note in. There is no name on it, only: “Willing to trade in kind, prices as the market goes, will call at the house.”

There are men like this in the valley every year at this time. They do not go to market. They go straight to the estates whose terms are nearly up.

The rate is worse than the market. But they come to you, and they cost you none of your time.
